title: Use of multimodal large language models for the assessment of thermal injuries based on clinical photographic documentation
summary:
Background: After a burn injury, it is essential for further treatment to judge correctly how deep the burn reaches into the skin and how large the burned area is. This determines whether a wound will heal on its own or needs surgery, and whether a patient should be transferred to a specialised centre for severe burns. Even experienced doctors often misjudge the depth. Modern artificial intelligence programs that can understand both images and text (so-called language models such as ChatGPT) are now easily accessible to almost everyone. Whether they can reliably assess burns from photographs has hardly been studied.
Research question: How well can such programs estimate the depth and size of a burn from photographs, compared with doctors and with the actual course of healing?
Methodology: We use photographs of patients who were treated for burns at the University Hospital Aachen between 2017 and 2026. The photographs were taken during routine care and are edited so that no person can be identified. Several artificial intelligence programs and doctors then assess the same photographs. Their assessments are compared with the actual course, i.e. whether the wound healed on its own or required surgery. We also examine how appropriate the programs' treatment recommendations are. No additional examinations are carried out on patients.
Aim: If the programs perform about as well as doctors at a burn centre, they could in future support the initial assessment, for example in emergency medical services or smaller hospitals.

interventions.name: Retrospective, single-centre, non-interventional diagnostic comparison study (single cohort, paired comparison within the same patients). Patients of all ages with thermal injuries (ICD-10 T20–T32) treated at the Department of Plastic Surgery, Hand and Burn Surgery, University Hospital RWTH Aachen,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Thermal injury (ICD-10 T20–T32, burns and corrosions) treated as inpatient or outpatient at the Department of Plastic Surgery, Hand and Burn Surgery, University Hospital RWTH Aachen, between 01 January 2017 and 01 June 2026
- At least one evaluable clinical wound photograph in the photo documentation system, taken within 48 h after the thermal injury
- Documented physician assessment of burn depth and burned body surface area
- Sufficient documentation of the clinical course to establish the reference standard (operative findings or healing course)
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing or insufficiently documented burn diagnostics, or reference standard not traceably documented
- Photographs of insufficient quality (e.g. blurred, obscured by dressings or blood, missing information on body location)
- Photographs in which complete anonymisation or masking of identifying image elements is not possible
- Objection to the scientific use of one's own data (§ 6 German Health Data Use Act, GDNG)
